summary: Careful, well-documented preregistered paired evaluation of a generate–validate–repair (GVR) wrapper around a single LLM (declared gpt-5-mini) for intent→configuration NetOps tasks (N=300 paired intents, shared-initial semantics). Execution and analysis artifacts (full provider traces, per-episode validator traces, scoring JSON, manifests, and hashes) are archived. Primary result: baseline 299/300 vs guarded 300/300; paired difference 0.00333; exact McNemar two-sided p=1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00,0.01]. Authors disclose ceiling effect, limitations of emulator/closed-world validator, single-model scope, and unassessability of H2 due to zero residual guarded failures. Overall methods, preregistration fidelity, bookkeeping, and reproducibility evidence are strong; conclusions are appropriately bounded.
optional_revisions: Add a single-sentence explicit note in Results clarifying why the exact McNemar two-sided p-value equals 1.0 given the observed discordant counts (n10=1,n01=0) to aid readers unfamiliar with small-sample exact tests (the analysis artifacts already archive test implementation and code).

In the Methods or Disclosure, add a cross-reference (path + SHA‑256) to the exact analysis code / script used to compute the exact McNemar test and bootstrap CIs so readers can reproduce the reported p-value and CI directly from the archived artifacts.

Briefly emphasize in Limitations that the shared-initial semantics isolates gate marginal effect but does not measure practical end-to-end pipelines where generator context or repeated generation could differ; point readers to the deterministic_reconciliation.json for the provider_call accounting details.
